intent: Let the user flip one independent on/off state with a control that looks and behaves like a button.
typical_uses: A toolbar button that stays pressed until pressed again (a formatting mark such as bold)
A button that flips one independent display or marking state on and off

dont_use_when.situation: A labelled settings switch whose change applies immediately
A set of related, usually mutually-exclusive options

instead.note: ToggleGroup holds the shared pressed state across its items.

dont_use_when.situation: A one-shot action with no pressed state

invariants.text: `pressed` and `defaultPressed` are both accepted; `defaultPressed` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `pressed` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

anti_patterns.dont: Render an icon-only toggle with no visible label or aria-label
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label` naming the action the glyph performs

a11y.by: Base UI's own Toggle primitive (a native button element carrying aria-pressed bound to the pressed state, with the button's own keyboard activation) plus toggle.test.tsx's own button-role and accessible-name assertions and its data-pressed assertions

onPressedChange.states: onPressedChange is a callback of the next pressed state and event details, not a plain change handler
onPressedChange.because: Base UI types the callback as `(pressed: boolean, eventDetails) => void`, where eventDetails carries the triggering event, its reason and controls for cancelling or allowing propagation; a function type has no JSON Schema representation, so nothing beyond its presence is asserted.

value.states: value is typed by the caller's own Value type parameter, not a plain string
value.because: `ToggleProps<Value extends string = string>` lets a caller narrow the value to its own literal union - the set of ids a ToggleGroup manages, typically. JSON Schema cannot express a type parameter, so only its base shape (a string) is asserted and the caller's own narrowing is checked by tsc, not by Ajv.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the toggle's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the toggle's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (pressed, disabled). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through toggle.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: Icon-only with no accessible name
bad.why: An icon-only toggle carries no accessible name of its own; without `aria-label` a screen reader announces nothing for the control.

bad.title: Several toggles wired by hand for an exclusive set
bad.code:
<>
  <Toggle pressed={view === 'grid'} onPressedChange={() => setView('grid')} aria-label="Grid">
    <GridIcon />
  </Toggle>
  <Toggle pressed={view === 'list'} onPressedChange={() => setView('list')} aria-label="List">
    <ListIcon />
  </Toggle>
</>
bad.why: This hand-rolls the exclusive selection ToggleGroup already holds, so use ToggleGroup instead.

capabilities.name: icon_only
capabilities.description: The toggle draws its glyph alone: it squares to its own size step (a 32px box at `sm`) and fixes the glyph at 18px regardless of the active size step, instead of the ordinary padded row a label sits in.

companions.typed_by: cva(...), returns (props: VariantProps<typeof toggleVariants> & { className?: string }) => string
companions.description: The variant/size class-name builder Toggle itself uses, exported so ToggleGroupItem can apply the identical classes to the Base UI Toggle it renders inside a group - kept here because Toggle has to exist before ToggleGroup can import it.

onPressedChange.description: TS: ((pressed: boolean, eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element | undefined; }) => void) | undefined. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc. onPressedChange is a callback of the next pressed state and event details, not a plain change handler. Base UI types the callback as `(pressed: boolean, eventDetails) => void`, where eventDetails carries the triggering event, its reason and controls for cancelling or allowing propagation; a function type has no JSON Schema representation, so nothing beyond its presence is asserted.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ToggleState> | undefined. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the toggle's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ToggleState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. Not expressible in JSON Schema, checked by tsc. style accepts a function of the toggle's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (pressed, disabled). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through toggle.module.css, not through this.

value.description: TS: Value | undefined. Not fully expressible in JSON Schema; what the type states beyond the kind above is checked by tsc. value is typed by the caller's own Value type parameter, not a plain string. `ToggleProps<Value extends string = string>` lets a caller narrow the value to its own literal union - the set of ids a ToggleGroup manages, typically. JSON Schema cannot express a type parameter, so only its base shape (a string) is asserted and the caller's own narrowing is checked by tsc, not by Ajv.
